description: The >>LISTING { ON | OFF } compiler directive (ISO §2023:7.3.18) - it turns any source listing on or off. §2023:7.3.18.3 GR1 makes producing a listing implementor-defined and directs that the directive be IGNORED when no listing is produced; WiseOwl COBOL produces none, so recognize-and-consume is the conforming disposition. The introduction gate rejects the directive word below 2002. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): COBOL-85 has no compiler directives, its only compiler-directing forms being statements (§1985:IV.6.4.2.2.1: 'The compiler directing verbs are COPY, ENTER, REPLACE, and USE'), so a '>>' line cannot occur in a conforming COBOL-85 source; ISO/IEC 1989:2002 introduces the directive (§2002:7.2.2 SR5: 'A compiler directive is composed of the compiler directive indicator') and §2002:F.2 lists the facility as a change, its item 29: 'Compiler directives instruct the compiler to take specific actions during compilation'. The directive is in the 2002 text: §2002:7.2.15.2 GR1: 'If the compiler does not produce a source listing, the LISTING directive shall be ignored'; and §2002:F.2 names it, its item 29: 'to control the source listing'. 2014 keeps it (§2014:7.3.16: 'The LISTING directive instructs the compiler to turn any source listing on or off') and so does 2023 (§2023:7.3.18.1).

directiveOperand.citation: ISO §2023:7.3.18.2 general format (rendered, folio 78): LISTING and OFF are underlined, ON is not, so per §2023:5.2.3 the ON alternative may be selected with the word omitted — which is the case §2023:7.3.18.3 GR4/GR5 call 'specifying or implying the ON phrase'. ⚠ The transcription's figure note reads the missing underline as a typesetting omission and would make the choice mandatory; the underlining plus GR4/GR5's 'implying' is followed here, because rejecting a bare >>LISTING would reject conforming source.

source:
>>LISTING ON
       IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. PB725LI.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           DISPLAY "X".
           STOP RUN.
